researchUpdates.title: Research on the mechanical properties and freeze resistance of geopolymer concrete
researchUpdates.publicationStatus: Published early-access accepted version; version of record pending
researchUpdates.authors: Zhiqiang Xing, Haiying Chen, Yongsheng Kang, Peng Wang and Baian Zhang
researchUpdates.summary: A kaolin–slag–fly-ash geopolymer concrete program varies precursor balance and alkaline activation, then adds mixed-length polypropylene fibers and evaluates age-specific compression and flexure alongside rapid freeze–thaw, salt-freeze, pore-structure and damage-model responses.
highlights: Fiber reinforcement is evaluated through both mechanical and exposure-specific measures, allowing retained dynamic modulus and mass change to remain distinct from compression and flexure.
The preferred formulation belongs to the tested precursor sources, activator settings, fiber lengths and accelerated freezing protocols; it is not a universal cold-region mix design.
researchUpdates.access: Primary Nature/Springer publisher metadata and early-access article-level evidence were reviewed. The accepted version remains subject to editorial change. Full raw data, replicate-level uncertainty, field placement and natural winter exposure were not independently audited. Compression and flexure are summarized only at reported ages; no tensile or shear strength is inferred, and the damage equation is not external validation.
researchUpdates.summaryBasis: Primary Nature/Springer publisher metadata, early-access article evidence, author information and version notice; no abstract text, publisher highlights, figures, tables or full-paper passages were reproduced

researchUpdates.title: Accelerated CO₂ curing of fly ash–GGBS self-compacting geopolymer concrete: experimental, environmental and explainable machine learning assessment
researchUpdates.publicationStatus: Published early-access accepted version; version of record pending
researchUpdates.authors: Herbert Sinduja Joseph, Siva Shanmukha Anjaneya Babu Padavala, Erick Saavedra Flores, Nelson Maureira-Carsalade, Abraham Mengistu Gashe and Siva Avudaiappan
researchUpdates.summary: Ten fly-ash/GGBS self-compacting geopolymer concretes compare ambient and accelerated CO₂ curing across fresh behavior, age-specific compression, splitting tension and flexure, transport and chemical exposures, microstructure, cradle-to-gate impacts and compressive-strength prediction.
highlights: The study combines measured performance, sequestration-related mass change and cradle-to-gate modeling, but each result retains its own functional unit and experimental or inventory boundary.
The machine-learning models predict compression within the assembled dataset; their reported fit does not independently validate flexural, tensile, durability or life-cycle outcomes.
researchUpdates.access: Primary Nature/Springer publisher metadata and early-access article-level evidence were reviewed. The accepted version remains subject to editorial change. The program contains ten laboratory mixtures, while life-cycle results depend on the selected inventory and boundary and the machine-learning assessment depends on its dataset and validation design. Field curing, long-term carbonation, reinforcement corrosion and external model transfer were not demonstrated.
researchUpdates.summaryBasis: Primary Nature/Springer publisher metadata, early-access article evidence, author information and version notice; no abstract text, publisher highlights, figures, tables or full-paper passages were reproduced

journalArticle.title: One study can have several evidence boundaries
journalArticle.summary: Two new multi-method studies show why mechanical, durability, environmental and predictive claims should remain connected but not interchangeable.
paragraphs: The freeze-resistance study links mixture and fiber choices to mechanical tests, accelerated cycling, salt exposure, pore observations and a damage equation. The carbon-curing study spans fresh behavior, several strength modes, transport and chemical exposures, sequestration indicators, life-cycle inventory and machine-learning prediction.

For the catalog, record each test age, exposure, response variable and modeling boundary separately. A good compressive result does not establish flexural, tensile, freeze–thaw or environmental performance, and a high predictive fit inside one dataset is not independent experimental replication.
